discover.intro: Rates are ratios with units: miles per hour, pages per day, dollars per pound. One famous trap waits today.

problem.q: You drive to a town 60 miles away at 30 mph and come back along the same road at 60 mph. What was your average speed for the whole trip, in mph?
problem.sol: Going takes 2 hours, returning takes 1 hour: 120 miles in 3 hours is **40 mph**, not 45. You spent more *time* at the slower speed, so it counts more.

sections.md: 45 mph (the average of 30 and 60) is the tempting answer, and it's wrong. Average speed is always **total distance ÷ total time**. The slow leg lasts twice as long, so it pulls the average down.

**Distance = rate × time**, and its two rearrangements: rate $= \frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}$, time $= \frac{\text{distance}}{\text{rate}}$. Keep units visible: $\frac{\text{miles}}{\text{hour}}\cdot\text{hours} = \text{miles}$.

sections.title: Average speed with unequal distances
sections.problem: Sasha runs 6 km at 12 km/h, then walks 2 km at 4 km/h. What is her average speed?

steps.md: Running time: $6\div 12 = 0.5$ h. Walking time: $2\div 4 = 0.5$ h.
Total: 8 km in 1 h, so 8 km/h.

sections.md:
### Work rates
"Pat paints a fence in 3 hours" means Pat's rate is $\frac13$ fence per hour. **Rates add when people work together**, not times. If Sam paints a fence in 6 hours (rate $\frac16$), together they paint $\frac13 + \frac16 = \frac12$ fence per hour, so the job takes 2 hours.

item.q: One pipe fills a pool in 4 hours, another in 12 hours. Together, how many hours to fill it?

sections.title: Closing speed
sections.problem: Two cyclists start 45 miles apart and ride toward each other at 12 mph and 18 mph. When do they meet?

steps.md: The gap shrinks by $12 + 18 = 30$ miles every hour.
steps.ask: Why can we add their speeds?
steps.why: In one hour, one covers 12 miles of the gap and the other covers 18, so together 30 miles of gap disappear each hour.

sections.md: Avery reasoned: "Ana mows a lawn in 2 hours and Ben in 4 hours, so together it takes $\frac{2 + 4}{2} = 3$ hours."
sections.question: What is wrong?
sections.explain: Together they must be faster than Ana alone (2 hours), so 3 hours can't be right. Rates: $\frac12 + \frac14 = \frac34$ lawn per hour, so $\frac43$ hours.

sections.prompt: A plane flies from A to B with a tailwind and back with the same wind against it. Explain why the round trip takes longer than it would with no wind at all.
sections.model: The slow leg (into the wind) takes extra time, and the fast leg saves less time than that, because you spend *longer* on the slow leg. Time per mile is $\frac1{v}$, and slowing down by $w$ adds more time than speeding up by $w$ saves.

item.q: Convert 90 km/h to meters per second.

summary: $d = rt$. Average speed = total distance ÷ total time, never the average of the speeds.
For jobs, rates (jobs per hour) add; times don't.
Objects moving toward each other close the gap at the sum of their speeds.

items.q: A train leaves at 9:40 and travels 210 miles at 70 mph. When does it arrive? Give the minutes past noon.
items.sol: 3 hours: arrives at 12:40, so 40 minutes past noon.

items.q: If 6 workers build a wall in 10 days, how many days would 4 workers take (same rate each)?
items.sol: The wall is 60 worker-days; 4 workers need 15 days.

items.q: Jo walks up a stopped escalator in 60 seconds. Standing still on the moving escalator takes 40 seconds. How many seconds does it take to walk up the moving escalator?
items.sol: Rates in escalators per second: $\frac1{60} + \frac1{40} = \frac{2 + 3}{120} = \frac1{24}$. So 24 seconds.

items.q: A car averages 40 mph for the first half of a trip's **distance**. How fast must it go for the second half to average 60 mph overall?
items.sol: Say each half is 120 miles. First half: 3 hours. To average 60 over 240 miles you need 4 hours total, leaving 1 hour for 120 miles: 120 mph.

items.q: At 3:00 the hands of a clock form a 90° angle. How many minutes after 3:00 are the hands first on top of each other?
items.sol: The minute hand moves 6° per minute and the hour hand 0.5° per minute, so the minute hand gains 5.5° per minute. It must gain 90°: $90\div 5.5 = \frac{180}{11}\approx 16.4$ minutes.
hints: How many degrees per minute does each hand turn?

reteach.md: **Another way: make a table.** For trips with legs, list each leg with distance, rate, and time in columns. Fill in what you know, use $d = rt$ across each row, then add the distance column and the time column. Average speed is the distance total over the time total.
If the problem says "together," add rates, not times.

cards.front: Average speed for a round trip at speeds $a$ and $b$?
cards.back: $\frac{2ab}{a + b}$: total distance over total time. It is less than $\frac{a+b}2$.

cards.front: Two workers take $a$ and $b$ hours alone. Together?
